ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)

protocol_overview.type: Synchronous serial half-duplex 2-wire debug protocol; host-driven SWCLK plus bidirectional SWDIO; strict 46-bit transaction format (8-bit Request + 1-bit Turnaround + 3-bit ACK + 33-bit Data + 1-bit Turnaround) per AP/DP register access; APnDP + RnW + A[2:3] select the target register.
protocol_overview.duplex: half-duplex per cycle on SWDIO with explicit 1-bit Turnaround periods between host-driven and target-driven phases (Request and Data-Write are host-driven; ACK and Data-Read are target-driven).
wire_names_optional: nTRST (only in SWJ-DP variants exposing TRST)
SWO (separate trace pin, not part of SWD protocol)
protocol_overview.controller_role: Debug host (USB-to-SWD probe such as J-Link / ST-Link / CMSIS-DAP) drives SWCLK out and bidirectionally drives or tri-states SWDIO; sequences 46-bit transactions; sets the SELECT register for AP+bank addressing; reads RDBUFF to recover the final posted read.
protocol_overview.target_role: Target SoC implements SW-DP (or SWJ-DP) at the wire layer + DP register set + one or more APs (MEM-AP, JTAG-AP, etc.); decodes 8-bit Request, drives the 3-bit ACK, and either drives the 33-bit read data + parity (for reads) or samples the 33-bit write data + parity (for writes).

functional_requirements.text: The SWD interface shall provide two dedicated pins: SWCLK (host-driven clock) and SWDIO (bidirectional data). The SWJ-DP variant additionally accepts JTAG-style 4-pin operation via the same pads (TCK→SWCLK, TMS→SWDIO, TDI/TDO unused-in-SWD-mode).

Each SWD transaction shall consist of exactly 46 bits in this order: 8-bit Request (host-driven) + 1-bit Turnaround + 3-bit Acknowledge (target-driven) + 32-bit Data + 1-bit Data Parity + 1-bit Turnaround.

The 8-bit Request packet shall be: bit0=Start (always 1), bit1=APnDP (0=DP, 1=AP), bit2=RnW (0=Write, 1=Read), bit3=A[2], bit4=A[3], bit5=Parity over APnDP+RnW+A[2:3], bit6=Stop (always 0), bit7=Park (always 1). Transmitted LSB-first on SWDIO synchronous to SWCLK rising edges.

The 3-bit Acknowledge field shall encode one of: OK=001, WAIT=010, FAULT=100. All other 3-bit patterns are reserved or indicate a protocol error. OK means the target accepted the request; WAIT means the target is busy and the host must retry; FAULT means a sticky error has occurred (host must read CTRL/STAT, write ABORT, then retry).
The 32-bit Data field shall be transmitted LSB-first synchronous to SWCLK rising edges. The 33rd bit shall be the even/odd parity of the 32-bit data (single-bit parity over the 32 data bits).

Two 1-bit Turnaround periods shall be present in every transaction: one before the ACK (allowing SWDIO to switch from host-driven to target-driven) and one after the Data field. The number of turnaround cycles is governed by CTRL/STAT.TRNCNT and defaults to 1.

The Debug Port (DP) shall implement at minimum the registers IDCODE/DPIDR (0x0, read), ABORT (0x0, write), CTRL/STAT (0x4), SELECT (0x8, write), and RDBUFF (0xC, read). ADIv5.1+ adds TARGETID, DLPIDR, EVENTSTAT in higher banks selected via SELECT.DPBANKSEL.

Up to 256 Access Ports (APs) may be present in a single DAP; the active AP is selected by SELECT.APSEL[31:24]. Each AP exposes 64 bytes (16 × 32-bit registers) at offsets 0x00..0x3C, banked by SELECT.APBANKSEL[7:4] for higher-address registers; IDR and BASE are at fixed offsets 0xFC and 0xF8.

The canonical AP shall be MEM-AP, exposing: CSW (0x00, Control/Status), TAR (0x04, Transfer Address), DRW (0x0C, Data Read/Write), BD0-BD3 (0x10-0x1C, Banked Data), MBT (0x20, Memory Barrier Transfer), CFG (0xF4, Configuration), BASE (0xF8, ROM Table base), IDR (0xFC, Identification). Reads/writes via DRW use the current TAR value as the system-bus address.

AP reads shall be posted: the ACK of read N returns the OK/WAIT/FAULT status for read N-1 and the host receives the read-N-1 data with the ACK of transaction N+1 (or via DP.RDBUFF if N is the final read). A read of DP.RDBUFF flushes the posted-read queue and returns the most recent read data.

When the target returns WAIT (010), the host shall retry the same request after one or more SWCLK cycles. The host shall not interpret the data field of a WAIT-ACK transaction. WAIT retries are not counted against any maximum retry limit at the protocol layer (host policy decides).

When the target returns FAULT (100), one or more sticky error bits in CTRL/STAT have been set (STICKYORUN, STICKYCMP, STICKYERR, WDATAERR). The host shall read CTRL/STAT to identify the cause, write ABORT with the corresponding clear bits (ORUNERRCLR / STKCMPCLR / STKERRCLR / WDERRCLR), then retry the failed request.

A line-reset sequence — at least 50 consecutive SWCLK cycles with SWDIO held HIGH — shall return the SW-DP to a known reset state. After line reset the host shall perform a fresh DP IDCODE/DPIDR read on the first transaction.

An SWJ-DP-equipped target shall accept the JTAG-to-SWD selection sequence (16-bit pattern 0xE79E shifted on TMS/SWDIO after at least 50 cycles of TMS=1) to switch from JTAG mode to SWD mode; and the SWD-to-JTAG selection sequence (16-bit pattern 0xE73C) to switch back. The selection sequences must be preceded by a line reset in the current mode and followed by a line reset in the new mode.

The 32-bit IDCODE/DPIDR register (DP offset 0x0 read) shall identify the DP: DPIDR.DESIGNER[31:28] reads the JEP106 manufacturer ID, DPIDR.PARTNO[27:20], DPIDR.MIN[16] (min DP version), DPIDR.VERSION[15:12], DPIDR.REVISION[3:0]. The post-reset host's first transaction shall be an IDCODE/DPIDR read.

MEM-AP shall support auto-increment of TAR controlled by CSW.AddrInc[5:4]: Off (no increment), Single (TAR += transfer size after each DRW transfer), Packed (TAR increments by packed-mode rules — multiple 8/16-bit transfers per 32-bit DRW). Auto-increment must wrap correctly at 4 KB or 1 KB boundaries depending on the AP.

ADIv5.2 multi-drop SWD: the bus shall support multiple targets sharing SWDIO/SWCLK with per-target selection. After line reset the host issues a JTAG-to-SWD selection sequence followed by a TARGETSEL transaction; only the target whose DLPIDR.TINSTANCE+TARGETID.TPARTNO matches the TARGETSEL value drives ACK on subsequent transactions until the next line reset.

configurations.name: Pure SWD-DP target
configurations.description: The SoC implements only the 2-pin SW-DP variant — no JTAG support — SWCLK + SWDIO are the only debug pins.

configurations.name: SWJ-DP target
configurations.description: The SoC implements the mode-switchable SWJ-DP — supports both SWD (2-pin) and JTAG (4-pin) on the same pads; mode is selected at runtime via the 16-bit selection sequences.

configurations.name: Multi-drop SWD
configurations.description: Two or more SWJ-DP targets share SWDIO/SWCLK on a single 2-wire connector; selected per-target via DP TARGETSEL after the host's JTAG-to-SWD sequence (ADIv5.2+).

configurations.name: Single-MEM-AP DAP
configurations.description: A DAP with exactly one MEM-AP exposing a single system-bus (typical Cortex-M0/M0+ implementation).

configurations.name: Multi-AP DAP
configurations.description: A DAP with multiple APs — typical Cortex-A or multi-core SoCs have one MEM-AP per CPU + JTAG-AP for legacy IP + APB-AP for CoreSight peripherals.

error_response_conditions: ACK=WAIT (010) — target busy; host must retry the same request. Not a sticky error; CTRL/STAT is not affected.

ACK=FAULT (100) — one or more sticky error bits set in CTRL/STAT: STICKYORUN (overrun on a posted read), STICKYCMP (compare mismatch with DLPIDR), STICKYERR (AP transfer error), WDATAERR (data parity error during a write). Host must read CTRL/STAT, write ABORT clear bits, retry.
Protocol error — ACK pattern other than OK/WAIT/FAULT (e.g. all-0s if SWDIO stuck-low, or 111). Host should perform a 50-cycle line reset and re-IDCODE-read.
Data parity error on write — target sets WDATAERR in CTRL/STAT; subsequent transaction returns FAULT; the write is discarded.
Data parity error on read — host detects the mismatch locally; not signaled by the target. Host should retry (typically via another DRW read or RDBUFF read).
TARGETSEL mismatch (multi-drop ADIv5.2) — target ignores subsequent transactions; the addressed target drives ACK and bus normally. Host must re-issue line reset + TARGETSEL with corrected ID.
compliance_requirements: Both mandatory pins SWCLK and SWDIO shall be present, with SWDIO bidirectional.
Every transaction shall be exactly 46 bits in the order Request + Turnaround + ACK + Data + Parity + Turnaround.
The 8-bit Request packet shall have Start=1 (bit0), Stop=0 (bit6), Park=1 (bit7); Parity is even-parity over APnDP+RnW+A[2:3].
The 3-bit ACK shall be OK=001, WAIT=010, FAULT=100 (no other valid encodings).
Data shall be transmitted LSB-first synchronous to SWCLK rising edges; the 33rd bit shall be the parity of the 32 data bits.
Turnaround periods shall be at least 1 SWCLK cycle each (configurable up to a few cycles via CTRL/STAT.TRNCNT).
A 50-SWCLK-cycle SWDIO-HIGH line reset shall return the SW-DP to a known state from any state.
Reading IDCODE/DPIDR shall be the host's first transaction post-reset.
MEM-AP shall implement CSW + TAR + DRW + IDR + BASE at minimum; CFG and BD0-BD3 are mandatory for IDR.SizeSupported indicators; MBT and packed-increment are optional.
If an SWJ-DP is implemented, both 16-bit selection sequences (JTAG-to-SWD = 0xE79E and SWD-to-JTAG = 0xE73C) shall be recognized.
